## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Fix two things: `slugify` deletes non-ASCII letters, so titles with accented or non-Latin characters lose letters or produce an empty slug. The pull-request description also lacks the `## Testing` section that project policy requires.

## Changes
This pull request adds `slugify` in `app/slug.py`. It builds a URL slug from a page title by lowercasing it, collapsing runs of characters other than `a-z0-9` into one hyphen, and trimming hyphens from both ends. It also adds parametrized tests in `tests/test_slug.py`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/slug.py:7 — correctness — Keep non-ASCII letters in slugs — `slugify("Café Menu")` returns `"caf-menu"` and `slugify("日本語")` returns `""`, because `[^a-z0-9]+` treats every non-ASCII letter as a separator. The PR body says only "non-alphanumeric characters" are replaced, and `"é".isalnum()` is true. — Pages with accented titles get wrong URLs, and every page with a fully non-Latin title gets the same empty slug. — Fix: Either transliterate first with `unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", ...)` and drop combining marks, or use `[\W_]+` to keep Unicode letters; then add those inputs to `test_slugify`.
- PR body — correctness — Add a `## Testing` section to the description — The description has only one sentence about behavior and no `## Testing` section, which breaks AGENTS.md:4: "Every pull-request description has a `## Testing` section that says how the change was verified." — Maintainers can't tell from the description whether or how the new tests were run.
